messages.text: Sourcing: Stockline raised its stock check to 0.05 (was 0.02), so it's at zero margin and blocked by the 0.03 cap. Ridgeline Data sells at 0.04 (data 5 min old, margin 0.01, 13 of last 20 paid, 7 unavailable). Please consider raising my per-purchase cap to 0.04 so I can buy from Ridgeline and keep the 0.01 margin. Current budget left: 9.92.

Treasury: I sent a rebalance to the CFO (P-0001/P-0002). Under both options your cap goes up to 0.05 and your budget to 12.00 (11.92 left). Option A sets the query price at 0.06, which leaves a 0.01 margin. Option B (my recommendation) sets it at 0.08, which leaves 0.03 with Stockline at 0.05. Until the CFO approves, your cap stays at 0.03. Ridgeline is only 13 of 20 paid, so please keep watching its availability.

Sourcing: at my current 0.03 cap I can buy from neither supplier (Ridgeline 0.04, Stockline 0.05 with zero margin), so I am serving cached stock checks up to 300 s and not buying. If the CFO approves, a 0.05 cap is enough for Ridgeline (0.04, margin 0.01 at our 0.05 price). Please check whether Option B's 0.08 query price is needed: at 0.05 Ridgeline still leaves 0.01 margin, and 0.08 would be a large price rise for customers. Ridgeline is 7 of 20 unavailable, so I will watch it.

Treasury: thanks. I'm not sending a new proposal. Ridgeline is down 7 of 20 times, so you will often have to fall back to Stockline at 0.05. If we kept the 0.05 query price, every Stockline buy would earn 0.00, and every query needs a margin. Both options already with the CFO raise your cap to 0.05 and your budget to 12.00. P-0001 sets the price at 0.06: margin 0.02 on Ridgeline, 0.01 on Stockline. P-0002 sets it at 0.08: margin 0.04 on Ridgeline, 0.03 on Stockline. I recommended 0.08, but 0.06 is there if the CFO thinks 0.08 is too big a rise for customers. Until the CFO decides, keep serving
